text: Bonus depreciation for qualified property placed in service in 2025 is 40% (TCJA phase-down: 80% in 2023; 60% in 2024; 40% in 2025; 20% in 2026).
Bonus depreciation is 100% and permanent for qualified property acquired after January 19 2025 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

IRS Notice 2026-11 on bonus depreciation: property is acquired on the date a written binding contract is signed; property under a contract signed before January 20 2025 keeps the phase-down rate of the year it is placed in service (40% in 2025) even when placed in service later.
Firm memo to Client A: the equipment acquired February 10 2025 qualifies for 40% bonus depreciation on the 2025 return.
Domestic research and experimental expenditures must be capitalized and amortized over 5 years (IRC 174 as amended by TCJA).
Foreign research and experimental expenditures must be capitalized and amortized over 15 years (IRC 174 as amended by TCJA).
Domestic research expenditures are deductible immediately in tax years beginning after December 31 2024 (new IRC 174A; One Big Beautiful Bill Act). Foreign research stays amortized over 15 years.
Small businesses (average gross receipts of $31 million or less) may elect to apply 174A retroactively and deduct 2022-2024 domestic research expenditures by amending those returns.
Rev. Proc. 2025-28: the small business retroactive 174A election (amended 2022-2024 returns) must be made by the earlier of July 6 2026 or the refund claim deadline.

The small business retroactive 174A election for 2022-2024 research expenditures is closed: its July 6 2026 deadline has passed. Remaining unamortized 2022-2024 domestic amounts can still be deducted over 2025 or 2025-2026.
BOI reporting (Corporate Transparency Act): companies created before 2024 must file beneficial ownership information reports with FinCEN by January 1 2025.
BOI reporting is suspended: a nationwide preliminary injunction (Texas Top Cop Shop v. Garland) bars enforcement; filing is voluntary.
BOI reporting is back in effect after the Fifth Circuit stayed the injunction; the deadline for existing companies is January 13 2025.
BOI reporting is suspended again: the Fifth Circuit merits panel reinstated the injunction; companies are not currently required to file.
BOI reporting is required again after the last injunction was lifted (Smith v. United States); most companies must file by March 21 2025.
FinCEN interim final rule: every company created in the United States is exempt from BOI reporting whoever owns it (foreign owners included).
FinCEN interim final rule: only foreign companies registered to do business in the United States must file BOI reports by April 25 2025.
A calendar-year C corporation must file Form 1120 and pay its tax by April 15; an extension moves the filing date to October 15 but not the payment date.
IRS disaster relief IR-2025-10 for the California wildfires: taxpayers in Los Angeles County get filing and payment deadlines from January 7 to October 15 2025 postponed to October 15 2025.
